The ladder

His ruler, read off the verdict files on disk when this page was built. On each public set the organism is measured against a model alone and a null, then against the published rows those verdicts keep with their sources: first the local-model bar, then the frontier bar. Beside accuracy sits where the answers came from: a model call in seconds, cells with no model call in microseconds, one direct lookup in nanoseconds. Every number is a field of a verdict file: hover it, or tap it, to see the file and the field path. A sample is marked partial with its size, and a verdict that is not on disk reads not measured.

Its statement

The ask path of act/prompt.mjs now tries a direct table first and the knowledge tier before any model cell. On the 200 held-out first-sentence facts of the knowledge bar's draw (seed knowledge-draw-2026-09-23), asked through ask() with the model cell offline, 122 were answered correctly at recall@1 with provenance memory or direct and no model call (61.0%, the bar is 100); 176 came from the direct table in one lookup, and 176 of those 176 gave the answer the tier alone gave. The same questions scored 122 with the tier alone, 122 with a control table that holds every title but the drawn ones (0 direct hits), 0 with the tier and the table off, and 18 when the answer is the title's own last word. The table memoises the tier: it was filled by asking the tier "What is <title>?" for 284749 titles, the drawn titles among them, and none of the hidden sentences was ever in the store. After one unrecorded warm pass, native answers took a mean 42.6 microseconds a whole ask with the table on, 1806.4 with the tier alone and 1475 with the control table. Over 1000000 lookups a run the table took a median 70.92 ns a hit and 25.75 ns a miss, measured with process.hrtime.bigint on a shared machine. The tasks suites scored 724 of 725 before and 724 of 725 after, and of the 724 suite questions ask() answered exactly and correctly before the change, 0 were lost with the table off and 0 with it on. The semantic tier is now bounded by a declared 256 MB byte budget, room for 15416 named keys, instead of 4,096 keys.

Its statement

One organism-year is declared to be one generation of the whole population on a plane (64 children, 64 evaluations), so organism-years equal generations. On the grid plane the loop ran 502,991 organism-years in 300.000 s and the searched best's score on the fresh draw grid/velocity:heldout, which the loop never searched or read, went from 49 to 148 of 160, 196.823 tasks gained per million organism-years; its first plateau was at 0.400 s (the searched score last rose before it at 0.100 s), and it grew 4 times by widening, 120 by ingesting a new draw and 545 by spawning. That fresh score first reached its highest, 152, at 136.321 s and never went higher; from half the wall to the end it moved by -3. On the synthetic plane it ran 690,928 organism-years in 300.000 s and went from 89 to 256 of 256 on years/synthetic:fresh0, 241.704 per million organism-years, first plateau at 0.400 s. At the grid run's measured 1676.6 generations per wall second, one billion organism-years would take 596,433 s (165.7 h): a projection, not a measurement. With growth off (the control, 300 s) the grid plane went from 49 to 109 on the same fresh draw. The bar's fresh seeds were printed during development (a 3 s smoke run at a 2000 ms window, before the 250 ms window was chosen; development.barSeedExposures names every run that saw them). The machine was shared with other builders, so every rate is a contended wall-clock rate; no model was called.

The daily ruler

Four columns on a seed that is the date, so no day's items can be memorised; the composite is their mean. His target is a rise of five to ten percent a day.
